evidence: Compared git diff HEAD against the HEAD blob of MyAccessibilityService.kt: the nine try blocks of the base survive the split one for one across AccessibilityTree, KmOverlay, PicapOfferCloser and WhatsAppResponder, the only two dropped functions were findWindowRoot and the empty handlePossiblePicapPopup, and the throttle, policy, overlay and close bodies are statement for statement identical apart from the tag constant and windows being passed as a parameter.

Traced every close pipeline exit end to end: waits are 200 then 400 then 600 ms, the loop stops at three attempts or on CLOSED or CV_RENDERED, pendingCloseId is cleared only when it still equals the scheduled order, provider failures and empty or stale windows return NO_POPUP or NO_OFFER inside that bound, and the sole try in the file wraps the provider call while flattening, parsing and clicking stay unguarded.

Checked the remaining areas: throttle constants and its five state fields are byte identical to HEAD and touched only from onAccessibilityEvent on the main thread, every KmOverlay entry point runs on main and the close path posts through a main looper Handler, SavedLocationManager.findMatch only reads SharedPreferences and parses JSON with no network from the same main thread call site as HEAD, and no CoroutineExceptionHandler, removeCallbacks or onUnbind exists anywhere in app src main.

findings.location: picap/PicapOfferProcessor.kt handlePicapEvent line 40 and provider lambda picapWindowsProvider in MyAccessibilityService.kt line 51
findings.claim: The windows accessor now runs as the argument of the provider lambda, ahead of the only try left on that path, so a throwing or null getWindows escapes handlePicapEvent and onAccessibilityEvent uncaught and kills the process instead of degrading to the empty list skip that HEAD returned. The narrowing is still latent rather than immediately reachable, so this stays WARNING rather than worse: AccessibilityTree.logWindows at MyAccessibilityService line 170 evaluates the same accessor first with no guard, exactly as HEAD line 211 did, and would already have crashed on the same failure before line 40 is reached.
proof_refs: HEAD MyAccessibilityService findAllWindows returned inside a try that catches Exception, logs findAllWindows error accediendo windows and returns an empty list, so the accessor was covered at that site

Staged PicapOfferProcessor.handlePicapEvent line 40 calls the provider with no try, while AccessibilityTree.findAllWindows keeps its try only around the mapNotNull loop, so both the accessor and the non-null parameter check of the callee run outside any guard

PicapOfferCloser.attemptNonCvClose lines 86 to 91 wraps the same provider in a try and returns NO_POPUP on failure, whereas MyAccessibilityService line 170 calls AccessibilityTree.logWindows with the accessor unguarded before the package routing at line 176, mirroring HEAD line 211

findings.location: whatsapp/WhatsAppResponder.kt processWhatsAppText line 146 and pasteAndSend lines 234, 260, 271; MyAccessibilityService.kt onDestroy lines 120 to 127
findings.claim: onDestroy cancels the shared service scope, hides the overlay and dismisses the popup, but never removes the main looper callbacks the WhatsApp pipeline posts, so the delayed auto accept and the paste retry chain can still fire after teardown against a disconnected service. Every one of those posts is byte identical to HEAD, so the gap is pre-existing rather than created by the split.
proof_refs: WhatsAppResponder line 146 posts a delayed lambda on a freshly constructed main looper Handler, pasteAndSend line 234 builds another Handler and schedules retries at lines 260 and 271, and no removeCallbacks call exists anywhere under app src main
HEAD MyAccessibilityService contains the same posts at lines 605, 686, 712 and 723 with no removal either
MyAccessibilityService onDestroy lines 120 to 127 only hide the overlay, cancel the scope, dismiss the popup and null the instance, and neither revision overrides onUnbind

findings.location: picap/PicapOfferCloser.kt scheduleNonCvClose line 51 and attemptNonCvClose lines 96 to 130
findings.claim: The retry loop runs in a launch child of a SupervisorJob scope with no CoroutineExceptionHandler and only the window read is guarded, so an exception from flattening, parsing or clicking reaches the default Android handler, terminates the process and skips the pendingCloseId clear at the end of the loop. Nothing introduced by the split widens this: empty or stale windows, a failed click and a vanished popup all finish inside the three attempt bound and clear the id, and the id survives only when the scope is cancelled at service destroy, when the instance is going away anyway.
proof_refs: PicapOfferCloser line 51 launches on the injected service scope and the file has no try around the content flattening, the parse or the close click, the only try being the provider wrapper at lines 86 to 91

A search of app src main finds no CoroutineExceptionHandler and no uncaught exception hook, and HEAD declares the same CoroutineScope with SupervisorJob and Dispatchers.Default with the same unguarded loop at lines 1369 to 1392

The clear at PicapOfferCloser lines 67 to 70 runs after the loop in every non throwing exit, attempts are capped at 200, 400 and 600 ms, and the id is cleared only when it still equals the scheduled order so a second schedule cannot be wiped

findings.location: picap/PicapOfferCloser.kt NON_CV_CLOSE_DELAY_MS line 15, delay computation line 57 and attemptNonCvClose lines 108 to 124
findings.claim: The first close attempt fires 200 ms after detection, so if the Cruz Verde service node has not rendered yet the parsed service field reads empty, the X click discards a genuine offer and the terminal CLOSED outcome ends the pipeline with no recovery. Only a failed click leaves attempts 2 and 3 able to abort on CV_RENDERED once the node appears. HEAD already carries the same 200 ms constant and the same delay formula, so this is the documented residual of the requested timing and is pre-existing relative to the base.
proof_refs: PicapOfferCloser line 15 sets NON_CV_CLOSE_DELAY_MS to 200 and line 57 waits NON_CV_CLOSE_DELAY_MS for the first attempt then that value times the attempt number, giving 200, 400 and 600 ms, while HEAD line 119 declares the same 200 ms value and the same formula

PicapOfferProcessor lines 127 to 136 schedules the close whenever the parsed service field is empty and the popup carries an Aceptar marker, and attemptNonCvClose lines 108 to 111 only aborts when a later re read finds the Cruz Verde node already present
The comment at PicapOfferCloser lines 13 and 14 states the wait exists to give the popup time to render the Cruz Verde service node, which is exactly the race that 200 ms leaves open
